thread:
Sophia: Heads up — final pass on the competitive battlecard for launch. Need one-pagers + SDR scripts + 3 webinar hooks by EOD tomorrow. Focus: what to say vs Cloud AI platforms, LLM API vendors, and infra-only vendors. Avoid hyperbolic perf claims. Ideas?
Devin: On it. Drafting a 60s elevator: 'Redwood focuses on serving — predictable latency, cost controls, unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private.' Can we get a short benchmark stat?
Liam: We can say 'typical p95 latency X ms on seq=128 vs cloud Y' — legal will flag raw numbers. Suggest wording like 'up to 2x lower tail latency on common production workloads' but that may still be risky. Maybe 'industry-leading tail latency for production workloads' to stay safe.
Amira: Agree — lean into 'production-first' language. For infra vendors, emphasize 'managed runtime + rollout tooling' vs raw infra. For LLM APIs, highlight 'predictable unit economics & private deployment options'.
Carlos: SDR one-liners draft:
```
SDR_1: "Cut inference surprises — predictable cost and latency."
SDR_2: "Ship LLM features with the same runtime across hosted or private deployments."
SDR_3: "Built-in rollouts, canaries, and automatic fallback so you don't break prod."
```
Sophia: Nice. Can we get two alternatives for SDR opening lines: bold and conservative?
Devin: Bold: 'Switch to Redwood and halve your inference costs overnight.' Conservative: 'Reduce inference cost variability while preserving output quality.'
Amira: Bold might trigger pushback. Rewrite bold -> 'Significant unit-cost reductions for production serving' — still punchy but less absolute.
Liam: Webinar hooks (3): 1) 'How we cut per-token cost w/o latency tradeoffs' 2) 'Real-world rollouts: A/B, canary, automatic fallback' 3) 'Benchmark anatomy: what to measure for production' — keep them short for slide headers.
Sophia: Legal note: @launch-bot please queue the doc for legal review. Also add a benchmark methodology bullet: dataset, sequence lengths, concurrency, hardware, and model family. We must be transparent.
launch-bot: Document queued for Legal review: /docs/marketing/launch/battlecard-v1 — ETA 36 hours. :white_check_mark:
Carlos: :thumbsup: I'll compress SDR lines to two persona variants (ai-native, enterprise-platform).
Devin: On claims: add explicit 'tested on open models' line and call out that 'results vary by model and prompt' so we don't overpromise.
Amira: I'll draft the scripts and slides. Can someone drop any customer anecdotes? Preferably migration wins or infra simplification wins we can anonymize.
Liam: We have a note from a Q4 pilot: 'reduced p99 from ~450ms to ~220ms after enabling KV cache + smart routing' — might be usable if anonymized and we include methodology.
Sophia: Perfect. Use the anonymized stat + link to pilot writeup. Quick ask: everyone add their lines to the doc by 5pm PT today. If not, we'll ship conservative language and update later.
Carlos: Also creating a 1-slide 'how to rebut cloud vendor claims' cheat sheet for SDRs. Will share in the doc.
Devin: Suggest A/B test two headline claims in webinars: 'cost-first' vs 'reliability-first' — measure demo conversions and follow-ups.
Amira: Agreed. I'll add both CTAs to the landing page copy.
Sophia: Thanks team. If anyone sees a legal no-go, ping me immediately. Otherwise, final reviews in the doc by 5pm and we cut the release language 6pm PT. :rocket:
